title: The Rubric as a promptfoo Config
description: A promptfoo configuration that states the judge as data: a prompt, an echo provider, a judge model, three rubric assertions, and the dataset.

steps.description: This is `promptfooconfig-rubric.yaml`. The page says the no-code path says the same thing in a configuration file: here are the outputs, here is the judge, here are the assertions. The header comments name the file and the judge, `ollama llama3.2` at temperature 0.
`prompts` points at `file://prompt.txt`, the one-line template that echoes each stored answer straight through.
`providers` is `echo`. With the echo provider nothing generates a fresh reply, so the judge grades your dataset rather than a newly generated answer.
`defaultTest` sets the judge that grades every assertion. Its `provider` is `ollama:chat:llama3.2`, the comment calling it the judge model that grades every `llm-rubric` assertion.
The `assert` list holds three `llm-rubric` assertions, one per criterion: `claims_cited`, `directness`, and `counterargument`. Each `value` states a PASS and a FAIL condition in plain text.
`tests: file://dataset.csv` supplies the rows to grade. The page says `dataset.csv` holds one row per sample with columns `id` and `answer`.
